newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greece takes part in Cyprus military exercise.
newsitem.headline: Greece takes part in Cyprus military exercise.

text.p: Greek naval and air forces will take part in an annual military exercise in Cyprus starting on Friday, Cypriot defence officials said on Thursday.

More than 8,000 Greek Cypriot reservists will also take part in the exercise, codenamed Nikiforos, which ends on October 9, Brigadier-General Demetris Farsaris, chief of staff of the Cyprus National Guard, told reporters.
"Air and navy forces from Greece will take part," Farsaris said, adding that one of the purposes of the exercise was to test reservists on defence systems.

The exercise, to be carried out with live ammunition and air raid attacks on mock targets, runs at the same time as one by the Greek armed forces between Cyprus and Rhodes, codenamed Toxotis and due to begin on Sunday.
Cyprus has a defence pact with Greece, its closest ally. Athens pledges to come to the aid of Cyprus in the event of further hostilities with Turkey on the island.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkish troops invaded the north in 1974 days after a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup inspired by the military regime ruling Greece at the time.
Some 30,000 mainland Turkish soldiers are stationed in northern Cyprus, declared a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in 1983 and recognised only by Ankara.
